title: Local secrets, typed configuration and named connector bindings

nodes.summary: Checkout-local per-KB named secret store, never in Git
nodes.detail: Each KB in a checkout has its own key/value secrets, independent of plugins, outside the accepted root, evolutions and Git; no global fallback, cross-KB lookup or synchronisation. Configuration names keys as ordinary text (no SecretRef type), and secret values are never candidate capture inputs.
sections: Decision / Configuration remains ordinary typed root data

realised.evidence: PR #122 implements the per-KB ignored store and CLI

nodes.summary: Guest getSecret request returns plaintext; plugin builds its own auth
nodes.detail: The guest SDK exposes a typed GetSecret request composed with HTTP; trusted plugins receive the plaintext value and construct provider-specific authentication themselves, with no host injection or provider classification. Effectful evolution entries could use it via acquisition plugins.

realised.evidence: No guest secret request existed when seq 97 removed it pending a real consumer

nodes.summary: Host SecretStore plumbing scoped to selected KB, actionable missing-key errors
nodes.detail: Secret access is a host plumbing effect whose runner receives the selected KB's store scope; missing keys yield SecretNotFound naming the key (never the value), storage corruption is an operational failure, and there are no per-plugin grants, opaque handles or connection registry.

realised.evidence: PR #122 adds SecretStore capability and native interpreter

nodes.summary: Per-plugin root config files hold instances as generated Dhall union
nodes.detail: Connector instances live in a per-plugin root file (root/plugins/config/<plugin>.dhall) as a list keyed by a Kyyn-generated union of advertised connector config types derived from Haskell; Kyyn owns the envelope, plugins own payload schemas, and malformed config fails the whole root with no partial loading.
sections: Decision / Configuration remains ordinary typed root data

realised.evidence: PR #100 derives the union schema and loads root/plugins/config instances, rejecting invalid configs root-wide

nodes.summary: Pure per-instance config validator runs during root checking
nodes.detail: Each connector type supplies `validateConfig :: Config -> ValidationReport`, run on every configured instance during root checking with plugin/instance diagnostics; failure blocks acceptance, and it never fetches, reads secrets or tests credentials.
sections: Decision / Configuration remains ordinary typed root data

realised.evidence: PR #100 generates pure validator adapters and combines reports with root validation

nodes.summary: Plugins own provider authentication; no kernel Connection model
nodes.detail: Provider-specific authentication and response handling live in integration code using host capabilities; there is no kernel Connection entity, automatic credential injection or closed auth taxonomy, and required user actions are explicit, never hidden prompts in scheduled work.
sections: Decision / Authentication belongs to the integration

realised.evidence: PR #147 ships plugin-owned Graph client-secret and device-code auth with no kernel auth model

nodes.summary: Instances declare a binding; Kyyn.Connectors exports typed handles
nodes.detail: Each configured instance names an author-facing `binding`; Kyyn generates a Kyyn.Connectors module exporting a typed handle per instance (no payload or secret) so KB code calls e.g. Mail.viewEmail Connectors.salesMail. Bindings are unique valid identifiers; renaming one never changes instance identity or evidence.
sections: Decision / Configuration remains ordinary typed root data

realised.evidence: Binding validation lands in PR #100; PR #107 generates instance handles and proxies for KB tools

nodes.summary: Raw RootOpening carries config bytes; PrepareRoot compiles and validates
nodes.detail: RootOpening carries plugin config files as bytes without compiling plugins (for scaffolding and Before comparisons); PrepareRoot inspects declarations, decodes every instance and retains compiled validators, and ValidateRoot combines their reports. Neither probes a provider.
sections: Decision / Configuration remains ordinary typed root data

realised.evidence: PR #100 implements prepared-root wiring with this split

nodes.summary: Generated per-connector proxy modules with phantom-typed instance handles
nodes.detail: Proxies are generated as Kyyn.Plugins.P_<plugin>.<ConnectorType>; the exported Instance is phantom-typed by plugin and connector type so handles cannot be passed to another connector's methods.
sections: Decision / Configuration remains ordinary typed root data

realised.evidence: PR #107 generates phantom-typed proxies and instance bindings

nodes.summary: Guest secret requests deferred until a real consumer exists
nodes.detail: The first implementation is the host store plus local setup commands; guest request algebras are added only with actual consumers rather than as unused SDK constructors, and evolution execution stays pure (no secret-using acquisition inside evolutions).

realised.evidence: Design-only step removing guest Secrets from the spec; code had none, so it conforms immediately

nodes.summary: Secrets stored as plaintext Dhall files under .kyyn/secrets with CLI
nodes.detail: Each value is a hermetic Dhall Text at <kb>/.kyyn/secrets/<name>.dhall, explicitly plaintext at rest with ordinary permissions and an ignore rule; SecretStore gains write/list/remove; `secret set/list/remove` work without a valid schema, compiler or evolution, refuse empty input and never print values.

realised.evidence: PR #122 implements the store and CLI

nodes.summary: Masked secret show and kb.dhall marker required for secret commands
nodes.detail: `secret show` returns a masked value (first four characters for long values, true length preserved) in human and JSON forms; secret commands require root/kb.dhall in the selected directory so a wrong working directory cannot silently acquire secrets.

realised.evidence: PR #122 implements masked show (owner follow-up) and the marker check

nodes.summary: Source connectors read and replace secrets via guest requests
nodes.detail: Graph introduces the guest secret consumers: source and login programs can read secrets and replace them (e.g. refresh-token rotation) through ADR 0009's request rows, writing to the same per-KB store as local setup.

realised.evidence: PR #147 adds getSecret/putSecret to the guest SDK host row and per-KB persistence

nodes.summary: Explicit connector login entry; fetch never starts interaction
nodes.detail: A connector may advertise `login :: Config -> PluginLogin (Either LoginError ())`, invoked only by `plugin connector login PLUGIN INSTANCE` with accepted config; it fetches nothing and creates no evolution, and its secret writes are local setup.
sections: Decision / Authentication belongs to the integration

nodes.summary: Graph plugin owns client-secret and device-code auth with refresh rotation
nodes.detail: One microsoft-graph plugin owns GraphAuth (ClientSecret or DeviceCode) in its config; client-secret gets fresh .default tokens, device-code stores a refresh token and rotates it before proceeding, access tokens live per invocation, and the host knows nothing of tenants, scopes or endpoints.

realised.evidence: PR #147 implements both modes against a recording provider under GHC and MicroHs

nodes.summary: Shared Graph auth config with combined delegated scopes across connectors
nodes.detail: Calendar, Mail, Meetings and Files share one app registration; DeviceCode config carries the combined delegated `scopes` list so login consents for all and refresh never narrows it, with per-API permission requirements and explicit errors for unsupported auth/endpoint combinations.

realised.evidence: kyyn-v2 GraphAuth DeviceCode still has no scopes field and only the Calendar connector exists

editorial.note: Retargets the ADR 0014 cross-reference from historical selection to latest-only evidence; no change to bindings
Status update marking Graph auth implemented plus a sharedCalendar flag selecting the shared-read scope already described; realises 0016.13-15
Reconciliation: drops status/basis lines, restates host-side vs guest secret routes already covered by 0016.10/13, and points the decoded instance type at ADR 0015
Config example types switched from String to Text to match packed guest Text; no architectural change
Adds calendar windowStart/windowEnd config fields whose semantics are owned by ADR 0014; provider-config detail only

notes: The lane's most notable detour is guest secret access: the founding text gave plugins a GetSecret request, seq 97 removed it as speculative (host store + CLI only, evolutions pure), and seq 110/113 reintroduced read-and-replace guest requests once Graph needed token rotation. The ADR also grew in scope: retitled at seq 76 from 'Local secrets and plugin-owned authentication' to include typed configuration and named connector bindings, and later accreted a large Microsoft Graph authentication section that is really plugin-specific design living in a core ADR. Spec ahead of code: seq 151's shared combined-scope DeviceCode config and Mail/Meetings/Files permission rules are unrealised (code has no scopes field, Calendar only). The founding 'Trust and consequences' section carries real requirements (traces omit secret values and HTTP headers/URLs/bodies) but per the rules produced no node; worth a human check whether it should. Several small config-field steps (sharedCalendar, scopes String->Text, window fields) were judged editorial/provider detail rather than architecture.
